title: Bantu expansion spreads farming and iron
summary: Over two to three thousand years, Bantu-speaking farmers spread from West-Central Africa across most of central, eastern and southern Africa, carrying agriculture, cattle-keeping and iron-working. About a third of Africans speak Bantu languages today.

title: Nok terracottas and iron smelting
summary: The Nok culture produces striking life-size terracotta sculptures and some of the earliest iron smelting in West Africa.

title: Lapita voyagers reach Fiji and Tonga
summary: Seafarers of the Lapita culture, descendants of Austronesian migrants from Taiwan and the Philippines, sail into the open Pacific and settle Fiji, Tonga and Samoa — the ancestors of the Polynesians.

title: Modu Chanyu unites the Xiongnu
summary: Modu Chanyu seizes power and forges the first great steppe empire, which defeats the young Han dynasty and forces it to pay tribute.

title: Nalanda university founded
summary: Under the Guptas, the Buddhist monastery-university of Nalanda is founded; at its height it drew thousands of students and scholars from China, Korea, Tibet and Southeast Asia.

title: Aryabhata's astronomy and mathematics
summary: The mathematician-astronomer Aryabhata writes the Aryabhatiya, using a place-value number system, approximating pi to four decimals and explaining eclipses. Indian numerals, later carried west by Arab scholars, become the digits used worldwide.

title: First Turkic Khaganate founded
summary: Bumin Qaghan overthrows the Rouran and founds the Göktürk Khaganate, the first state to call itself 'Turk', which soon stretches from Manchuria to the Black Sea.

title: Dome of the Rock completed
summary: Umayyad caliph Abd al-Malik completes the golden-domed shrine on Jerusalem's Temple Mount, the oldest surviving major work of Islamic architecture.

title: Borobudur completed
summary: The Shailendra dynasty completes Borobudur, the world's largest Buddhist monument, a stepped mountain of stone with over 2,600 relief panels.

title: Chichén Itzá dominates the Yucatán
summary: As the southern Maya cities empty, Chichén Itzá becomes the leading power of the northern Maya, building the pyramid of El Castillo, whose stairs cast a serpent of light at the equinoxes.

title: Polynesians settle Hawaii
summary: Polynesian navigators, steering by stars, swells and birds, reach the Hawaiian islands — among the most isolated on Earth. (Dates for the first settlement range from about 900 to 1200.)

title: Avicenna's Canon of Medicine
summary: The Persian polymath Ibn Sina (Avicenna) completes the Canon of Medicine, which was used as a textbook in both the Islamic world and European universities for 600 years.

title: Mahmud of Ghazni sacks Somnath
summary: Mahmud, sultan of the Ghaznavid Empire based in Afghanistan, raids the famous Somnath temple — one of seventeen campaigns of plunder into northern India.

title: Rock-hewn churches of Lalibela
summary: King Lalibela of the Zagwe dynasty has eleven churches carved down into the living rock as a 'New Jerusalem'; they are still in use today.

title: Mongols destroy the Khwarazmian Empire
summary: After the Khwarazmian shah kills his envoys, Genghis Khan invades Central Asia and sacks Bukhara, Samarkand, Merv and Nishapur with enormous loss of life.

title: Rapa Nui's moai are carved
summary: Polynesian settlers of Rapa Nui begin carving nearly a thousand giant stone statues of their ancestors, the moai, and moving them across the island.

title: Polynesians reach Aotearoa (New Zealand)
summary: Polynesian voyagers in double-hulled canoes settle New Zealand, the last large landmass on Earth to be reached by humans; their descendants become the Māori.

title: Majapahit Empire founded
summary: Raden Wijaya uses a Mongol invasion force against his rivals, then drives the Mongols out and founds Majapahit, which under the minister Gajah Mada comes to dominate the Indonesian archipelago.

title: Ibn Battuta's travels
summary: The Moroccan scholar Ibn Battuta sets out on pilgrimage and keeps going for nearly 30 years — through the Middle East, East Africa, Central Asia, India, Southeast Asia, China and Mali — covering about 120,000 km.

title: Kilwa and the Swahili coast at their height
summary: Ibn Battuta calls Kilwa one of the most beautiful cities in the world. Swahili city-states along the East African coast trade gold, ivory and slaves for Indian cloth, Persian ceramics and Chinese porcelain.

title: Ulugh Beg's observatory at Samarkand
summary: Timur's grandson Ulugh Beg builds a huge observatory; his star catalogue was the most accurate since antiquity.

title: Haudenosaunee (Iroquois) Confederacy
summary: Five nations — the Mohawk, Oneida, Onondaga, Cayuga and Seneca — unite under the Great Law of Peace, a confederation with a council of chiefs chosen by clan mothers. (Its founding date is debated, from the 12th to the 16th century.)

title: Portuguese build Elmina Castle
summary: Portugal builds the first European fort in sub-Saharan Africa to trade for gold; Elmina later becomes a major hub of the Atlantic slave trade.

title: Kingdom of Kongo adopts Christianity
summary: King Nzinga a Nkuwu of Kongo is baptised after contact with the Portuguese; his son Afonso I builds a Christian kingdom that exchanges ambassadors with Lisbon and Rome.

title: Guru Nanak begins Sikhism
summary: After a spiritual experience, Guru Nanak begins preaching a faith of one God and the equality of all people — the founding of Sikhism.

title: Portuguese capture Malacca
summary: Afonso de Albuquerque seizes the Sultanate of Malacca, the great entrepôt on the strait linking the Indian Ocean and the South China Sea.

title: Transatlantic slave trade grows
place: West and Central Africa to the Americas
summary: The first direct slave voyages from Africa to the Americas begin around this time. Over the next three and a half centuries about 12.5 million Africans are forced onto ships; nearly two million die on the Middle Passage.
significance: The trade built the plantation economies of the Americas and devastated African societies; its legacies of racism and inequality endure.

title: Battle of Talikota
summary: The Deccan sultanates defeat the Vijayanagara Empire; its magnificent capital at Hampi is sacked and abandoned.

title: Spanish found Manila
summary: Miguel López de Legazpi makes Manila the capital of the Spanish Philippines. Its galleons carry American silver to Asia and Chinese silk back to Mexico — the first trade route linking every inhabited continent.

title: Battle of Tondibi
summary: A Moroccan army with firearms, sent across the Sahara, defeats the Songhai Empire, ending the last of West Africa's great Sahel empires.

title: Queen Nzinga rules Ndongo
summary: Nzinga Mbande becomes queen of Ndongo and spends four decades resisting the Portuguese slave trade and conquest through war and diplomacy.

title: Abel Tasman reaches Tasmania and New Zealand
summary: The Dutch navigator Abel Tasman sails south of Australia, sights Tasmania and New Zealand, and clashes with Māori — the first European contact.

title: Shivaji crowned Chhatrapati
summary: Shivaji, who led guerrilla resistance to the Mughals, is crowned king of the Maratha state, which grows into the dominant power in 18th-century India.

title: Osei Tutu founds the Asante Empire
summary: Osei Tutu unites the Akan states around Kumasi; tradition says the Golden Stool descended from the sky to symbolise the nation's soul.

title: Third Battle of Panipat
summary: Ahmad Shah Durrani's Afghan army defeats the Marathas in one of the largest battles of the 18th century, weakening the Indian powers just as the British East India Company expands.

title: Burmese destroy Ayutthaya
summary: After a 14-month siege the Burmese sack the Siamese capital, one of Asia's great trading cities. Taksin rallies the Thai and a new capital rises at Bangkok (1782).

title: Rebellion of Túpac Amaru II
summary: José Gabriel Condorcanqui, a descendant of the Inca rulers, leads a huge Indigenous uprising against Spanish colonial abuses; it is crushed and he is executed in 1781.

title: First Fleet arrives at Sydney Cove
summary: Eleven British ships carrying about 1,400 people, most of them convicts, found a penal colony — beginning the British colonisation of Australia and the dispossession of its Aboriginal peoples.

title: Usman dan Fodio's jihad founds the Sokoto Caliphate
summary: The Fulani scholar Usman dan Fodio leads a reformist jihad against the Hausa kings and founds the Sokoto Caliphate, one of the largest states in 19th-century Africa.

title: Kamehameha unites Hawaii
summary: Kamehameha I brings all the Hawaiian islands under one rule, founding a kingdom that lasted until the US-backed overthrow of Queen Liliʻuokalani in 1893.

title: Shaka builds the Zulu Kingdom
summary: Shaka reorganises the Zulu army and conquers his neighbours; the upheavals of this period (the Mfecane) displace peoples across southern Africa.

title: Battle of Ayacucho
summary: Antonio José de Sucre's army defeats the last major Spanish force in South America, securing the independence of Peru and the continent.

title: Trail of Tears
summary: Under the Indian Removal Act, the US Army forces the Cherokee from their homeland to Indian Territory (Oklahoma); thousands die on the way. Choctaw, Creek, Chickasaw and Seminole peoples suffer similar removals.

title: Treaty of Waitangi
summary: British representatives and over 500 Māori chiefs sign a treaty whose English and Māori versions differ on sovereignty — the founding document of New Zealand, and a source of dispute ever since.

title: Battle of Isandlwana
summary: A Zulu army armed mainly with spears and shields destroys a British column — one of the worst defeats of a colonial army by an African force. Britain conquers Zululand later that year.

title: Brazil abolishes slavery
summary: Princess Isabel signs the 'Golden Law', freeing about 700,000 enslaved people; Brazil, which had received the most enslaved Africans of any country, is the last in the Americas to abolish slavery.

title: Panama Canal opens
summary: After a failed French attempt and ten years of US construction, the canal links the Atlantic and Pacific, sparing ships the voyage around South America.

title: Federation of Australia
summary: Six British colonies unite as the Commonwealth of Australia.

title: Battle of Dien Bien Phu
summary: The Viet Minh under General Giáp besiege and capture a French fortress, ending French colonial rule in Indochina; Vietnam is divided at the Geneva Conference.

title: Bandung Conference
summary: Leaders of 29 newly independent Asian and African nations meet to oppose colonialism and stay out of the Cold War blocs — the seed of the Non-Aligned Movement.

title: The Year of Africa
summary: Seventeen African countries win independence in a single year, including Nigeria, the Congo and most of French West and Equatorial Africa.

title: Bangladesh wins independence
summary: After a brutal crackdown by the Pakistani army and a war in which India intervenes, East Pakistan becomes the independent state of Bangladesh.

title: Khmer Rouge take Phnom Penh
summary: Pol Pot's Khmer Rouge empty the cities and try to build an agrarian communist society; about 1.5–2 million Cambodians die from execution, starvation and forced labour.

title: Soviet invasion of Afghanistan
summary: Soviet troops invade to prop up a communist government and fight a decade-long war against mujahideen guerrillas backed by the US, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia.
